role: Independent agent; not workflow author or command-stub collector. Saved-only review; no workflow or target execution.
findings: One job-level expression determines the string boolean used by both tool preparation and bundle selection. Manual dispatch selects PGO only for typed pgo=true; its default is false. Pull requests select PGO only for the dedicated charlie/codex-oriole-pbs-pgo- head-prefix family, as explicitly requested by root. Other eligible PBS PRs retain the normal branch.

The opt-in installs the selected stable toolchain llvm-tools-preview component, resolves llvm-profdata from that compiler sysroot with quoted paths, requires executable presence and fetches locked GNU-target dependencies before the existing offline PGO pipeline. The bridge subsequently verifies compiler/profiler LLVM version agreement and actual compilation flags.

The false branch preserves the exact normal prepare.py command. Existing PBS revision, runner, read-only permissions, pinned actions, validator, full XML checks, installed identity, glibc 2.17 follow-up and timeout remain unchanged.

Artifact retention selects pgo/latest.json and pgo/runs only, excludes .a/.so/.dylib entries, and never selects sibling pgo/targets. It retains raw/merged profiles, generated fixtures and training records, logs and manifest/artifact hashes.

All previously reviewed bridge/pipeline implementation and test bytes remain unchanged after the worktree restack. The new workflow is an explicit opt-in release path, not evidence that stable PGO distribution execution has succeeded.

saved_validation.scope: YAML parse, unchanged runner and independent gates, bash -n for all run steps, false/true argument flow with inert command stubs; no Cargo/compiler/parser/container/workflow execution.

publication_note: Requested narrowing of the new prose claim that an exact static archive remains in the installed distribution: before that distribution is built/read back, the established fact is that the bundle manifest retains its exact archive hash. This does not block the workflow source.
limitations: Manual/default/PR event routing was reviewed in source; saved stub tests cover shell argument flow and quoted paths, not GitHub event execution.
The local Ohm result does not establish production stable compilation or final installed archive/TLS/glibc/strict XML/benchmark outcomes.
